html:
SMTO-EXE-0067 — SMTO can't reach the clipboard on the Gateway computer

GUID: e21b7a21-16c3-52dc-b4ed-a88296f88dfd
Slug: clipboard-no-session
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • Copy and paste belong to a signed-in desktop. The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer, isn't running inside a signed-in desktop, so SMTO can't use its clipboard. The clipboard wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Sign in to the desktop of the Gateway computer and leave that user signed in and switched to, not locked out by another user. The clipboard only exists inside a signed-in desktop, so there must be one for SMTO to use.
  2. Ask the person who manages the Gateway to start it from that signed-in desktop, not as a background service or over a remote text-only connection. A Gateway started in the background can't see the desktop's clipboard even when someone is signed in.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a new task. A new task picks up the Gateway's clipboard abilities as they are after the restart.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads or sets the clipboard on that computer without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway computer's operating system (Windows, macOS or Linux), to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't paste passwords or private text onto that computer's clipboard while testing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Clipboard readiness found no interactive desktop for the Gateway process: the Linux display or compositor connection failed, the macOS session is not on the console, or Windows has no accessible input desktop (for example session 0).

What this means

  • Clipboard readiness could not establish access to the current interactive desktop: Linux session connection failed, macOS lacked an on-console session or Windows lacked an accessible input desktop. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Clipboard readiness could not establish access to the current interactive desktop: Linux session connection failed, macOS lacked an on-console session or Windows lacked an accessible input desktop.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the Gateway account's interactive session and backend connectivity without reading clipboard content.

How to fix it

  • Run the Gateway inside the logged-in user's desktop session: on Linux with a reachable DISPLAY (X11) or WAYLAND_DISPLAY socket under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, on macOS in the active console session, and on Windows in the interactive user session rather than as a session-0 service. On X11 the readiness probe also reports no session when python-xlib cannot be imported by the Gateway's Python, so confirm it is installed. Then restart the Gateway, refresh its metadata and start a new task.
  • Log in to the selected Gateway desktop and run the Gateway in that session.

Retry and execution caution

  • Log in to the selected Gateway desktop and run the Gateway in that session.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended Gateway reports clipboard capabilities from the correct interactive session.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
